title: Soil-nailed wall in clay (Amherst test wall)

meta.title: Soil-nailed wall in clay (Amherst test wall)
meta.notes: 6.1 m vertical cut in undrained clay (Su = 25 kPa) with two nail rows at 20° (tensile 118 kN, plate 86 kN, bond 15 kN/m, spacing 1.5 m; axial, passive) and the facing weight as a line load; the critical plane printed by a commercial program, from the toe (0, 0) to the crest (6.279, 6.1), 44.2°.

source.derived_from: cSlope verification problem V083 (MIT License), https://github.com/ZilanCiftci/cslope
notes: Sheahan (trial wedge) 0.887; program D 0.899 on the earlier input (6 m wall, plane at 44.5°).

Wall height 6.1 m and plane from commercial program A's critical surface (Fig. 47.2: left and right slope intercepts (0, 6.100) and (6.279, 6.100)); the figure labels (0, 6) and (11, 6) are rounded, as everywhere in that manual. Before this correction the wall was 6 m high and the plane ran to (6.106, 6): cSlope 0.899 (+1.0 %); now 0.885 (-0.6 %). Sheahan & Ho (2003), Table 1, give the Amherst wall 6.1 m high, with nails 1.5 m apart both ways at 20°, head 86 kN, tensile 118 kN, bond 15 kN/m and shotcrete 14.6 kN/m, as here.
